Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Head of Search), Priya Desai (ML Engineer), Liam O'Neill (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Acme is exploring embeddings + reranking to improve product search relevance and customer support retrieval.
- They currently use a hybrid of Elastic + a homegrown nearest-neighbor index; evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated for latency and cost.
- Key concerns: throughput (peak qps), vector dimensionality (they're using 1536), hybrid search (keyword + vector), data residency and VPC, SOC2/KMS.
- Agreed next steps: send integration patterns, pilot proposal, and pricing for Dedicated.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- Embedding dimensionality and model selection
- Vector DB integration patterns (hosted connectors vs push to customer DB)
- Throughput/latency targets and benchmarking
- Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick intro and then dig into your current search stack and what you're trying to accomplish.
[00:07] Carlos Vega: yeah thanks, Carlos here. we run search for product discovery and support articles, current infra is elasticsearch plus a custom ANN layer, it's kinda brittle.
[00:16] Maya Lin: cool, and just to set expectations, I'm Maya on the SE team, I'll cover architecture and benchmarks. Jordan will cover commercial and next steps.
[00:25] Priya Desai: quick note, our embeddings are 1536 dims produced by a distil-embedder pipeline, we can sample data after the call.
[00:33] Liam O'Neill: hi, probably gonna ask about latency at peak and how to do hybrid search with keywords plus vector scores.
[00:41] Jordan Hayes: perfect. so timeline, are you looking for a pilot in the next month?
[00:45] Carlos Vega: yeah Q1 would be ideal, we want measurable lift on relevance and not increase cost too much.
[00:51] Maya Lin: on technical fit, couple of patterns we see: 1) Redwood Hosted embeddings + Redwood-managed vector store, 2) Redwood-managed embeddings + push vectors to your DB (e.g., Pinecone or your Weav) 3) Dedicated or private where we run the runtime in your VPC or on-prem and you keep vectors local.
[01:10] Priya Desai: right now we need the vectors to remain in our VPC for regulatory reasons, so option 3 is interesting but we also care about throughput.
[01:18] Jordan Hayes: under that constraint Dedicated in a VPC peering or Redwood Private are typical. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools we run, Private gives you the control plane inside your VPC.
[01:29] Carlos Vega: can you explain the difference in practice for latency and ops?
[01:33] Maya Lin: sure, Dedicated is our reserved capacity with clear SLOs — better predictability on throughput. Private is full customer-managed deployment, so you manage networking and some infra updates, but you get data residency. Latency is mostly a function of where the GPUs are relative to your app. If it's inside your VPC or peered region, latency is comparable.
[01:49] Liam O'Neill: whats throughput like? Our peak is around 250 qps for vector search with reranking and bursts to 400.
[01:55] Maya Lin: that's totally plausible on Dedicated with an appropriate GPU pool and batching config. We typically advise continuous batching for high throughput and recommend warm KV cache for repeat prefixes to hit latency SLOs.
[02:08] Carlos Vega: ok, so batching doesn't blow up latency for tail requests?
[02:12] Maya Lin: good question; batching is workload-aware. you can set latency SLOs that avoid batching for low-latency routes; high-throughput routes batch more. We also have automatic fallback to smaller model variants if capacity is constrained.
[02:26] Priya Desai: about dimensionality — we're at 1536 dims using a mix of sentence-transformer style models. can you comment on storage and query cost impacts?
[02:34] Maya Lin: 1536 is common. Storage and vector search cost scale linearly with dim, but we offer quantization-friendly runtime and recommend 8-bit or product quantization in many cases to reduce storage without much accuracy loss. we'll give dimension-vs-cost examples in the doc.
[02:47] Jordan Hayes: and for reranking, do you plan to do a two-stage approach — first ANN recall then cross-encoder rerank?
[02:53] Carlos Vega: yes two-stage, but currently our reranker is too slow at scale. we want to move heavy rerank to a model optimized runtime or use a cheaper cross-encoder for top-k.
[03:02] Maya Lin: we see customers use a light-weight reranker (e.g., smaller cross-encoder) in the runtime to keep p95 low, and optionally offload deeper ranking offline. You can also use hybrid scoring: combine BM25 from Elastic plus vector score then rerank.
[03:18] Priya Desai: any out-of-the-box connectors to Elastic? we prefer keeping keyword index for filters.
[03:23] Maya Lin: we have documented patterns. integration is usually push vectors into your vector DB and keep Elastic for structured filters. For hosted customers we can push to Pinecone/Weaviate connectors; for Dedicated we can run the vector store co-located or have a connector that issues hybrid queries.
[03:38] Carlos Vega: competitor question — why not just use Pinecone?
[03:41] Jordan Hayes: fair. Redwood focuses on inference serving and reranking optimizations, plus deployment flexibility. We provide model-level control, quantization recommendations, and observability (per-token cost, latency breakdowns). Pinecone is great for vector storage but we give the full inference pipeline to handle rerank and model selection.
[03:58] Liam O'Neill: security items — are you SOC 2 and can we use our KMS?
[04:02] Jordan Hayes: yes SOC 2 in hosted; Dedicated and Private support BYOK with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 report and our security architecture doc.
[04:12] Priya Desai: what about model versions and rollback? we need canary rollouts.
[04:16] Maya Lin: we support rollouts — canary, A/B with automatic fallback to previous model variant. Also quality monitoring tied to prompts/evals so you can detect regressions.
[04:27] Carlos Vega: ok cost — do you have ballpark tco for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:31] Jordan Hayes: yes, will send a tiered estimate. Hosted is lower friction but can be more expensive at sustained high qps; Dedicated gives predictable unit cost; Private has higher setup but best for residency. We'll put numbers in the doc.
[04:46] Priya Desai: for benchmarking, what do you need from us?
[04:49] Maya Lin: sample queries and a representative document corpus, plus expected qps and p95 targets. If you're comfortable, share a sanitized sample of 50k-200k vectors and we'll run a smoke benchmark.
[05:01] Carlos Vega: we can provide 100k sample vectors, will sanitize.
[05:04] Jordan Hayes: perfect. we'll follow up with an intake form.
[05:08] Priya Desai: one more thing — we do some multi-lingual queries, does Redwood handle embeddings for that?
[05:12] Maya Lin: yes we support multi-lingual embedding models; model choice affects dim and cost. we'll recommend a model that balances coverage and dimension.
[05:22] Liam O'Neill: any caveats around hybrid search scoring — combining BM25 + vector scores is tricky to get right.
[05:26] Maya Lin: agreed, we recommend normalizing scores and using small calibration sets to tune weights; we can help with that during pilot.
[05:34] Jordan Hayes: recap and next steps: we'll send architecture doc, pricing, and a pilot proposal. SE will request sample data for a benchmark. Can we agree to target the pilot start the week of 2027-02-21?
[05:48] Carlos Vega: yes that works, subject to internal signoff.
[05:52] Priya Desai: I'll share the sample by EOD 2027-02-16.
[05:57] Jordan Hayes: great, we'll follow up with a calendar invite and intake form. thanks all.

End of transcript.
